- FintechCo wants assurance around what request/response data Redwood persists for hosted inference (request bodies, responses, HTTP headers, trace IDs) and the controls available to redact/mask PII before logs are stored.

- Default: Redwood stores structured request/response logs for troubleshooting and telemetry; by default PII is not automatically redacted unless configured.
- Options: request-side redaction hooks (customer-side), server-side masking rules, and a configurable retention policy per account/route.
- Technical specifics discussed: header capture config, trace-id preservation vs. full payload logging, and the ability to store only hashed identifiers.

Hi Marissa 

Thanks for the recap and the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying questions before we share sample payloads: 

1) Headers & trace IDs: We typically need trace IDs preserved to correlate requests across services. Can Redwood store trace IDs separately from request/response bodies (e.g., store trace_id and metadata but redact full payloads)?
2) Masking vs. redaction: Can we define masking rules that preserve schema (e.g., email -> *****@example.com, last 4 digits of account numbers) as opposed to full redaction?
3) Retention: What retention granularity is available  per-route, per-environment (prod/staging), and can it be <30 days for debug logs?

Also, curious about the process for validating that our PII patterns are fully covered (do you run test payloads through the mask engine and return a redacted sample?).

Thanks Amit  good questions. Looping in Neha from security engineering for technical confirmation; Monica from CS to coordinate the validation run and timeline. Answers below (high-level) and Neha will add technical details in a follow-up.

1) Trace IDs: Yes  we support storing trace IDs as separate indexed metadata while applying masking/redaction to payload storage. That lets you correlate traces without retaining full PII-containing payloads. You can opt to keep only the trace metadata and expiration shorter than payload retention.

2) Masking vs. Redaction: We support configurable masking rules that can preserve schema shapes (email partial-mask, numeric token-last4, hash-preserve). Masking rules are applied server-side via a ruleset file; we'll provide examples in sample-logging-config.txt. For extremely sensitive fields you can choose full redaction instead.

3) Retention: Retention can be set at route-level and environment-level. Options: 7/30/90/365 days, and we also support custom TTLs down to 1 day for debug logs in private/dedicated deployments. Hosted accounts can request sub-30-day retention and we'll provide a retention SLA in the contract (subject to account tier).

4) Validation: We run customer-provided test payloads through a non-production mask engine and return a redacted sample and a diff view showing what was changed. Monica will coordinate the test run and share instructions.

- Monica: schedule the validation run and share test-run playbook.
- FintechCo: send example payload(s) and a list of fields you want masked/redacted.

Hi Amit / Priya 

Following up with technical specifics and a sample config excerpt (see attached sample-logging-config.txt). Summary below: 

- Payload capture paths: Configure include/exclude rules by route (example: /v1/generate -> capture metadata only; /v1/debug -> capture full payload with masking).
- Header capture: Default headers captured: User-Agent, Content-Type, X-Request-ID. Optional capture for Authorization headers is strongly discouraged; we recommend stripping Authorization at the edge.
- Trace IDs: We persist trace_id as an indexed metadata field (string) separate from the payload store. Trace IDs are TTL-bound and can be exported to your logging system without payloads.
- Masking engine: Rule types supported: regex replace, JSON-path masking, partial-preserve masks (email, credit_card_last4), hash-preserve (sha256). Rules applied in order; sample order in config.
- Redaction logs: For audit we produce a redact-audit entry that notes which rule matched which field (does not contain original PII).

Example sample-logging-config.txt excerpt: 
\nroutes:
  - path: /v1/generate
    capture: metadata_only
    retain_days: 30
  - path: /v1/debug
    capture: payload
    retain_days: 7
    mask_rules:
      - json_path: $.user.email
        type: partial_mask
        pattern: "*@*"
      - json_path: $.payment.card_number
        type: last4_mask
      - json_path: $.headers.Authorization
        type: drop
\n
Validation flow we propose:
1) You provide 2-3 representative payloads (redacted identifiers ok).
2) We run them through Redwood staging mask engine and return redacted samples + redact-audit report.
3) We iterate on mask rules until you sign off.

Next steps:
- Please send one representative JSON payload and a short field-list of top-sensitive fields.
- Monica will set up the validation run; expected turnaround 48 hours from receipt of payloads.

If you'd like, we can also provide a short demo of the staging run on Thu 22 Jul.

Thanks,
